This function block is based on a template block provided by the Automation Framework. It is used to control a unit structured according to the ISA-88 standard, and manages unit mode and state transitions in compliance with PackML.
- Mode changes can be triggered via HMI commands.
- State transitions are controlled either by feedback signals from equipment modules (EMs) or by HMI commands.
Additionally, this block handles feedback from DC24V and pneumatic sources, which is an exception to standard state transition logic.

If simulation is active on a global level, inherit this status and set simulation active in this unit also. Information is written to DB ControlNodes, from where it is distributed to the equipmemt modules.

If acknowldge command on a global level is active, inherit this command and set acknowledge command in this unit also. Information is written to DB ControlNodes, from where it is distributed to the equipmemt modules.
If alarms are disabled on a global level, inherit this status and disable alarms in this unit also. Information is written to DB ControlNodes, from where it is distributed to the equipmemt modules.
If related safety zone is release, write this information into the ControlNodes DB as information for other modules
Provide the selected special functions to the underlaying equipment modules.
Add events here that trigger alarms and lead to the respective commands to the unit. It is possible to trigger alarms, set unit commands or do both for the specific event

Derive commands from the ProDiag supervision. The ProDiag supervisions contain categories which define the reaction of these supervisions (e.g. abort, stop, hold). These are handed over as commands to the unit level. Alternatively, if no ProDiag should be used, you can use the LAF_ManageBitAlarms to realize bit alarm handling. This block can be found in LAF in folder 70_AlarmHandling.
Collect the feedback from the unit level (commands) and all underlaying equipment modules (commands, stateComplete) and merge them. Handover one summarized set of commands to the interface manager.
Read the commands from all interfaces (process, local, hmi, remote) and merge them. Handover one summarized set of commands to the mode state manager.
Determine unit mode and state based on the collected commands and status

1. Read mode and state from the mode state manager an write them to the DB ControlNode 2. Read mode and state from the mode state manager, translate them to a string and write them in unitInterface 3. Determine if a mode change is allowed in the current state and write that information to the unitInterface
Update the mode and state history. When mode or state change occur, save current mode and state in history[0] and the previous ones in ascending order.
Determine the time that has been spend in modes and states.
Determine light behaviour based on current mode and stacklight configuration
Control the mode state manager remotely via OPC UA
Enable interfaces to control the unit
